title: IT Act s. 2(24) — Definition of "Income" (IT Act s. 2(24))

content.overview: Section 2(24) defines income inclusively. It lists profits, dividends, voluntary contributions, capital gains, winnings, and other enacted items. An inclusive definition adds to the ordinary meaning. It does not tax a receipt that the charging or exempting provision keeps out. A receipt is tested first as income, then under a head, then for an exemption.

cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?

enhancement.definition: Section 2(24) defines income inclusively. It lists profits, dividends, voluntary contributions, capital gains, winnings, and other enacted items. An inclusive definition adds to the ordinary meaning. It does not tax a receipt that the charging or exempting provision keeps out.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A receipt is tested first as income, then under a head, then for an exemption.
essentialIngredients: Not a capital receipt unless included
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The definition includes dividends, perquisites, capital gains, lottery and similar winnings, and specified gifts and benefits brought in by later clauses. A loan is not income merely because money is received. A capital receipt is not income unless the definition or a deeming provision includes it. The head of tax is section 14, not section 2(24).
examples: A cash gift is examined under the gifts clause of section 2(24) and section 56.
A loan repaid later is not listed as income.
A capital gain is income because the definition includes it.
